hood_desc: The town's main historic and tourist hub, centered on the famous WWII bridge and riverside restaurants.
A well-curated museum providing context on the Death Railway's construction and the POW and forced-labor history behind it.
Floating guesthouses and rafts along the River Kwai, offering a unique overnight stay directly on the water.

landmarks: Bridge over the River Kwai
The infamous steel-and-concrete bridge of the WWII Death Railway, built by Allied POWs and Asian laborers, still carries trains across the Khwae Yai.
Erawan National Park
A seven-tiered waterfall cascades through jungle into milky-turquoise pools where swimmers soak beneath limestone cliffs, Thailand's most beautiful cascade.
Death Railway and Tham Krasae Viaduct
Ride the surviving railway as it creaks along the wooden Wang Pho viaduct, clinging to cliffs high above the River Kwai Noi.
Hellfire Pass Memorial Museum
A moving Australian-built museum and walking trail through the deepest railway cutting, hand-hewn by POWs laboring by torchlight at terrible cost.
Kanchanaburi War Cemetery (Don Rak)
Immaculate lawns hold the graves of nearly 7,000 Allied prisoners who died building the Death Railway, a place of profound quiet.
Thailand-Burma Railway Centre
The definitive interactive museum opposite the war cemetery, unflinchingly documenting the railway's construction, its human toll and survivor testimonies.
JEATH War Museum
A bamboo-hut museum recreating POW camp conditions, its name drawn from the six nations entangled in the railway's tragic story.
Wat Tham Suea (Tiger Cave Temple)
A hilltop temple south of town where a giant golden Buddha and dragon-flanked staircases rise photogenically above emerald rice paddies.
Prasat Muang Sing Historical Park
The westernmost outpost of the Khmer empire, these 13th-century laterite temple ruins guard a bend of the River Kwai Noi.
Sai Yok Noi Waterfall
A roadside limestone waterfall near Nam Tok station where locals picnic and splash, a refreshing finale to the Death Railway train ride.

train.note: No international trains - the wartime Death Railway to Burma was dismantled beyond Nam Tok and never rebuilt. What survives is one of Thailand's most memorable rides: trains from Kanchanaburi cross the Bridge over the River Kwai and cling to the Wampo viaduct on the way to Nam Tok, about two hours. Services from Bangkok Thonburi station take around 3 hours. Fares are cheap and bought at the station.

bus.note: No international coaches - the Three Pagodas Pass to Myanmar is not a normal crossing for travellers. Buses and minivans from Kanchanaburi bus terminal reach Bangkok's Southern terminal in about 2-3 hours, plus services to Ayutthaya and Sangkhlaburi. Book through 12Go (https://12go.asia/).

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry. Longtail boats on the River Kwai run short trips between the bridge, the town and the riverside guesthouses, hired by the trip rather than timetabled, and raft-house stays are reached the same way.

full.name: Ayutthaya
full.blurb: The ruined former capital of Siam has brick temple towers and a headless Buddha statue entwined in banyan tree roots.

full.name: Damnoen Saduak
full.blurb: Vendors paddle narrow boats loaded with fruit and cooked food along canals at this long-running floating market.

notes.walk: The riverside area near the bridge and Walking Street is walkable; Erawan National Park and other waterfalls require a car, songthaew, or tour
notes.card: Accepted at larger hotels; cash preferred at markets and small guesthouses
notes.safety: Very safe town, popular with history-focused travelers and day-trippers from Bangkok. Very low crime.
notes.net: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier near waterfalls. Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes. ~$5-12 for a 10-15GB prepaid tourist SIM. Free wifi widely available. An AIS or DTAC tourist SIM or eSIM.
notes.transport: No airport in Kanchanaburi; Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK) in Bangkok is the main gateway. The historic Death Railway line connects Kanchanaburi to Nam Tok via the Wang Pho viaduct, plus regular service to/from Bangkok. Frequent buses and minivans connect to Bangkok (about 2-2.5 hr). Well connected via Highway 323 from Bangkok.
